utterance:
Samuel, from your story and the examination — pain that started around the belly button and moved to the lower right, feeling sick, off your food, a mild fever, and tenderness exactly over the appendix spot — I think it's very likely you have appendicitis, an inflamed appendix. This isn't something we can manage here; you need to go to the hospital emergency department today, now, to see the surgical team. They'll do blood tests and maybe a scan, and most likely you'll need an operation to remove the appendix. I'm going to phone the hospital and let them know you're coming, and I'll give you a letter.

Please don't drive yourself. We'll get you a taxi straight there, or a family member if they can come right away. Don't eat or drink anything from now on, in case you need surgery soon — that includes water. I won't give you anything stronger for pain here so the surgeons can assess you properly, but they'll give you pain relief at the hospital.

If on the way or while waiting the pain suddenly gets much worse or spreads across your whole tummy, you feel faint, very shivery, or start vomiting a lot, tell the staff immediately or call 000. The worry is the appendix bursting, which is why we don't wait. Does that make sense?
reply: Oh, right. An operation? Can I just go home and get my gear first?

utterance: I'd really prefer you go straight there. The longer we wait, the higher the chance it bursts, which makes things a lot more serious. Ring your mum or a mate to bring your phone charger and clothes to the hospital later — the important thing is you get there now.
reply: Alright, I will head straight there then.
